mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return correlation with FEDFUNDS is negative or insignificant (p-value > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic weakness and reduced consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month indicates strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive returns in more than 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions and economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines exceed 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL above 3.0%) triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST above 1000 thousand units) reflects robust economic activity and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return correlation with HOUST is negative or insignificant (p-value > 0.05) over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth (PAYEMS exceeding 0.5% month-over-month) indicates rising wages and consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signals stagflation risks, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL fails to produce negative returns in more than 40% of triggered instances.
